title: Check: stateful workloads
description: Five questions on running databases and friends.

questions.prompt: What does volumeClaimTemplates give a StatefulSet?

options.text: One shared PVC for all replicas
A separate PVC per replica, named after the Pod
An emptyDir per Pod
A ConfigMap per Pod

questions.explanation: data-web-0, data-web-1 and so on. Each Pod keeps its own volume across rescheduling.

questions.prompt: A StatefulSet Pod is deleted and recreated. What does it get back?

options.text: A new name and a new volume
The same name and the same PVC
The same name but empty storage
A random ordinal

questions.explanation: Stable identity is the contract: web-0 comes back as web-0 with data-web-0 attached.

questions.prompt: You scale a StatefulSet from 3 to 1. Which Pods go, and in what order?

options.text: web-0 then web-1
web-2 then web-1, in reverse ordinal order
Two at random
All three, then one is recreated

questions.explanation: Scale-down is reverse-ordered and one at a time, which is what lets a clustered database step down cleanly.

questions.prompt: Why does a database StatefulSet usually want a PodDisruptionBudget?

options.text: To speed up scheduling
So a node drain cannot take down enough replicas to lose quorum
To enable autoscaling
To encrypt the volumes

questions.explanation: `kubectl drain` respects a PDB; without one it will happily evict every replica at once.

questions.prompt: What is the practical warning about PVC deletion for stateful apps?

options.text: PVCs are deleted with the StatefulSet
They are NOT deleted with it, so old data lingers and can be silently reused
PVCs cannot be deleted
Deleting a PVC deletes the namespace

questions.explanation: Recreating a StatefulSet with the same name re-binds the old PVCs - convenient when you meant it, confusing when you did not.
